messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — fastpath compat scan tripped on a subset of infer nodes after the driver + CUDA rollout. Seeing OOMs and some cuDNN runtime errs. Also got a notification about CVE-2026-0001 affecting cuDNN: https://nvidiasec/2026-0001

jamal: Which nodes? can you paste the failing pod logs?

maria: p100-gpu-02 and a couple of a100s in us-west1. Log excerpt: ```RuntimeError: cuDNN kernel failure: convolution forward: cudnnStatusInternalError```. Happens at warmup, not every run.

eli: Did the scan include NCCL version mismatch checks? We've seen silent hangs when NCCL and driver mismatch.

maria: NCCL 2.18 on those nodes, driver 535.54, CUDA 12.3. The scan flagged ABI warnings for nccl and libcublas.

security-bot: CVE-2026-0001 (cuDNN) severity: 6.8/10. Impact: local code execution in rare crafted workloads. Patch available in cuDNN 9.0.2. Vendor recommends patch + driver combo validation.

jamal: If cuDNN patch is required, we need to check our signed-driver pipeline. Do we need to re-sign driver packages with customer KMS or rotate keys?

maria: We use internal KMS to sign build artifacts. The patch will be a patched cuDNN tarball shipped to our package repo; we sign the package with build-key. No customer KMS actions needed. But ops asked earlier about verifying KMS ACLs for the signing key — might be good to audit access.

ops-oncall: Noted. I'll run an ACL sweep on the signing key and post a short report. If we re-release drivers, we should log package-sign events to audit-log with the release id.

eli: Can we mitigate without immediate patch? Suggested temporary mitigations: 1) pin to previous cuDNN 9.0.0 on stable pool (fallback), 2) add a per-node guard to restart pods on kernel failure, 3) enable NCCL_DISABLE to force model parallel sync to CPU (performance hit).

maria: Agree. For immediate P0 mitigation: cordon affected nodes and move traffic to stable pool (cuDNN 8.x / driver 525). Can we do a canary rollback?

jamal: Yes — prepare a canary with 5 nodes in us-west1 with driver 525 + CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.4. I'll run a smoke job against that canary.

deploy-bot: create_release: canary-rollback-1853456789 created by jamal — targets: p100-gpu-xx (5 nodes), rollout strategy: canary 5 -> 50 -> 100, auto-rollback on 5% error threshold.

security-bot: Action items tagged: [A1] patch cuDNN to 9.0.2 and validate on canary; [A2] ACL audit for signing key; [A3] compatibility matrix update for driver 535.54 + CUDA 12.3; [A4] update runbook for node cordon + fallback.

maria: Triage priority: P1 for now (exploitable only under crafted workloads) but P0 for affected customers with latency-sensitive infer jobs. Recommendation: start canary rollback immediately, schedule cuDNN patch validation within 24h.

eli: I'll own validation tests (perf + functional) and add a short script to run the model warmup suite across driver/cudnn/cuda combos. Script snippet: ```#!/bin/bash
for drv in 525 535; do
  for cudnn in 8.4 9.0.2; do
    echo "test $drv $cudnn"
    ./run_warmup --driver $drv --cudnn $cudnn || echo "FAIL $drv $cudnn"
  done
done
```

jamal: Good. Once canary rollback is green, we'll schedule full rollback window and communicate to infra customers. Maria/ops: please prepare customer-facing blurb and internal postmortem template.

ops-oncall: Running ACL sweep now, will post results in 30m. Also adding audit-log hook for package-sign events (feature flag, rolling out to master).

maria: Thanks. I'll open a short incident ticket and assign tasks. If anyone sees additional nodes with cudnn errors, ping me and include node id. :mag: :white_check_mark:

eli: I'll kick off the validation CI and post results in this thread.

jamal: I'll monitor canary and attach metrics (oom count, kernel errors) to the release dashboard.

deploy-bot: release_update: canary-rollback-1853456789 status=IN_PROGRESS

security-bot: FYI — update the RBAC role for release engineers to remove write access from unapproved CI runners until ACL sweep completes.

maria: Acknowledged. Moving to action-mode.
